solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vamp never having time for leading lady

indicators.note: the woman must never have the letter, so every occurrence is struck out

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive woman, a temptress
T is the abbreviation for time, here removed both times it appears

explanation.surface: A film's star is cast as a seductress who never has a moment to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never having time' removes both Ts from TEMPTRESS, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman ruling an empire is the leading lady of the realm, a playful title-holder sense.

clue.text: Old bit of Lisbon that is toured by Brussels party

indicators.note: the EU and party travel around the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: Brussels houses the EU
sc. (scilicet) is the abbreviation meaning that is
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A Lisbon landmark is visited by a party from the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' means a coin, not a part of the city; 'toured by' signals that the EU and the party wrap round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal's coin before the euro was a currency unit, a piece of money once used in Lisbon.

clue.text: Saw dog restrained by lead

indicators.note: the dog is held in by the metal's symbol around it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a traditional dog's name

explanation.surface: Someone saw a dog held back on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for an old saying; 'lead' is the metal, not a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a traditional saying, a short piece of folk wisdom.

clue.text: Crank primarily collects money in Morecambe

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter

parts.note: a cent is a unit of money

explanation.surface: An odd character first collects money in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort; it is the comedian, giving ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an odd person with strange obsessions, an oddball.

clue.text: Nimble mole overcomes resistance

indicators.note: the spy comes over the letter, going around it

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: An agile burrowing animal pushes through the soil's resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' is the secret agent, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone lively and quick on their feet, especially in old age, so agile.

clue.text: Runway with struts?

parts.note: struts reads as supporting beams on an airstrip, but it is the models strutting along a fashion runway

explanation.surface: An airfield's landing strip built with structural supports.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests aircraft and engineering; the struts are actually the swaggering walks of fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised walkway at a fashion show is called a runway in American usage, and models strut along it.

clue.text: Stop work to phone Italian lady with Yankee

parts.note: to phone is to call
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth
Ada is a woman's name
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Knocking off work to ring an Italian woman and an American.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for ending the day's labour means to finish and go home.

clue.text: Star cast will include European stunner

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the abbreviation inside
to cast something is to throw it about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A film's star line-up will include a gorgeous European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges STAR to TASR; 'will include' puts E inside. 'stunner' is a stun gun, not a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric weapon that incapacitates people literally stuns them.

clue.text: Fan drier controls damp in odd places

indicators.note: the clothes frame holds the letters inside, keeping them in check

parts.note: an airer is a frame for drying clothes

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A fan heater's drier settings control dampness in strange spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in odd places' takes D and M from 'damp'; 'controls' puts them inside AIRER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiast or devotee, someone who looks up to another.

clue.text: Family owns a housing society in African capital

indicators.note: the family and ownership words give a home to the abbreviation inside them

parts.note: kin are family
to own something is to have it, so owns is has

explanation.surface: A family owns a housing association in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is a city in central Africa.

clue.text: PC rings about source of random artwork on farm

indicators.note: the word for the officer goes around the chosen letter

parts.note: a PC (police constable) is a cop

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: rings are circles

explanation.surface: A police constable investigates rings around some random farmland art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R, the first letter of 'random', inside COP.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterns flattened into fields of grain are a kind of land art, often hoaxed on farms.

clue.text: Crew's long hair cut

indicators.note: the hair is trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair

explanation.surface: A sailor's flowing locks get chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' is the verb here: to staff a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To crew a vessel is to staff it with sailors, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Chaperone in Madrid expected lady to come back

parts.note: something expected is due

indicators.note: the lady's name is read in the backward direction

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish chaperone awaits the return of a woman she is responsible for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' turns ANN into NNA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain an older woman who supervises a young lady is a traditional companion figure, a loanword.

clue.text: Taller ship picked up high priest

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: taller is higher, and an ark is a ship

explanation.surface: A lofty vessel collects a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' signals sound: HIGHER ARK said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief priest or senior church ruler holds top rank in a sacred order.

clue.text: Short county boxer's married, Breton style

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing the last letter

parts.note: Surrey is a county in south-east England
Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A boxer from an English county gets married in Brittany style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breton' is André Breton, the movement's founder, not Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: The artistic movement led by the French writer André Breton was dreamlike modernist art.

clue.text: Beachwear, sort of umber — unusual sort

indicators.note: a sort of umber is a reworked version of those letters

parts.note: the printed dash is spelt out as the word for itself

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: Summer clothing in an odd brownish shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges UMBER to BERMU; the dash gives DASH; 'unusual' rearranges SORT to ORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee-length casual trousers named after an Atlantic island are a classic holiday garment.

clue.text: Waves down close to front, a certain sign of cold weather

parts.note: to hail a taxi is to wave it down

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a certain one, a particular individual

explanation.surface: Someone flags down help as a cold front closes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' looks like a weather front; only its last letter T is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen lumps of ice falling from storm clouds are a marker of wintry conditions.

clue.text: Forecaster said supporting vineyard's a severe test

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting part sits below the other

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the prophetess's name gives a matching sound

parts.note: a sibyl was a prophetess who forecast the future

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster says supporting a vineyard is a tough trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A melting pot used for heating metals gives its name to any harsh trial of character.

clue.text: Check pink revised version

parts.note: to check is to rein in
a pink is a flower of the carnation family

explanation.surface: An editor checks the pink copy of a revised draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' is the flower, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reborn in a new body or form is a new edition of something old, a figurative fit.

clue.text: Cool leftie is upright person with confidential info

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: in a down entry an upright word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: A cool left-winger is an honest person who knows secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' turns RED IS into SIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation who knows its secrets is the classic source of privileged knowledge.

clue.text: Upset female carrying old books and old tool

indicators.note: the overturned word carries the other letters inside
in a down entry upset means turned upside down

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
lit is short for literature, books

explanation.surface: An upset woman carrying old books and an ancient implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns HEN into NEH.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone implement from the New Stone Age is an ancient prehistoric tool.

clue.text: Gambler showing improvement

definitions.meaning: in a more improved state, as in feeling well again

explanation.surface: A punter whose luck is on the up.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who wagers; the other is the comparative of good, meaning improved.

clue.text: Inspect boy covering over outstanding work

parts.note: to case a place is to inspect it, often before a crime

indicators.note: the boy goes around the cricket letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A boy covers for someone while unfinished work is checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' means still to be done, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount of pending cases a worker must handle is their load of jobs still waiting.

clue.text: It's clear police left uniform on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the first letters sit above the next part

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Plain-clothes police left their uniforms on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means easily understood, plain and transparent.

clue.text: He wrestled with oars, arriving here?

indicators.note: the letters are struggled with and twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rower battles with his oars to reach land.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat arriving at the coast ends on land, the place a rower reaches after the voyage.

clue.text: Grave, sort of square old doctor

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A solemn, old-fashioned doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like the adjective solemn; it is the noun, a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial vault or sepulchre is a resting place for the dead.

clue.text: Tender chicken for one, not rook

indicators.note: the chess letter is not included

parts.note: a chicken is one example of a bird
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Tender chicken for one, but no crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective about meat; it is the verb or noun for an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to offer, as one makes an offer at an auction.

clue.text: Axe poet describing Irish corn cutter

indicators.note: in crosswords describing can mean drawing around, so the outer words enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: to axe is to chop
an odist is a writer of odes, a poet

explanation.surface: An axe-wielding poet tells of an Irish farmer harvesting corn.
explanation.walkthrough: The corn is a hard patch on a foot, not a crop in a field; 'describing' means drawing a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot specialist removes corns, hard patches of skin, so is jokingly a cutter of them.

clue.text: Fashion model assuming a Republican title

indicators.note: the reworked word takes on the extra letters inside it
to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model takes on a Republican peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' rearranges MODEL to ELDOM; 'assuming' puts A and R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of a noble count is a hereditary title in the British peerage.

clue.text: Yak from heart of Tibet needing whip to avoid area

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
the whipping word must avoid the abbreviation, so it is dropped

parts.note: to leather someone is to whip them

explanation.surface: A Tibetan yak needs whipping to keep it away from a certain area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yak' is the verb, to chatter, not the animal. The middle letter of TIBET is B.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak is to chatter idly, and the Scots word for foolish talk means the same.
